Title: September 14, 2023 - Boulder City Council Study Session: Library District IGA Direction and 2024 Recommended Budget Discussion

Topic1.Title: Library District Intergovernmental Agreement and Board Appointment Process
Topic1.Summary: Staff briefed council on separating the municipal library from the city and transferring assets to the new Library District. Council gave direction to continue a hybrid trustee appointment process with a three-year check-in. Council also agreed to explore long-term leases for library buildings with a district-held termination option at five-year intervals.

Topic2.Title: Library Property Disposition Options
Topic2.Summary: Staff presented options for conveying or leasing city-owned library buildings and land, including Main Library, North Boulder, Carnegie, and Reynolds branches. Straw polls favored leasing the properties rather than conveying them. Council discussed lease length, reversionary interests, maintenance responsibilities, and natural disaster risk.

Topic3.Title: Community Connector Budget Engagement
Topic3.Summary: Community connectors Jamal Gilmore and Lenora Cooper presented findings from seven months of engagement with historically excluded communities. Top priorities included affordable housing, financial security and economic opportunity, and advancing racial equity. Council members thanked them and discussed mental health needs and future partnership.

Topic4.Title: 2024 Recommended Budget Overview
Topic4.Summary: Staff presented the 2024 recommended budget of about $514.8 million, with a general fund of $196.1 million. Key themes included behavioral health response, affordable housing investments, wildfire resilience, employee compensation, and a six-year capital plan of over $900 million. Staff noted revenue constraints, including a potential sales tax expiration and property tax ballot measure.

Topic5.Title: Public Safety, Homelessness and Behavioral Health Investments
Topic5.Summary: The budget includes funding for the CARE and co-response behavioral health programs, encampment management, and ambassadors and urban park rangers. Staff noted that unspent funds and pilot programs will be reviewed. Council members raised questions about the day services center and whether unspent funds could address urgent winter needs.

Topic6.Title: Capital Improvement Program and Community Culture Resilience and Safety Tax Projects
Topic6.Summary: Staff reviewed the six-year capital plan of about $900 million, highlighting the Western City Campus, East Boulder Community Center renovation, fire station replacements, and Civic Area and Pearl Street Mall projects. Debt service for Western City Campus would increase from $3.6 million to $6.1 million annually.

Topic7.Title: Street Maintenance, Potholes and Snow Removal Concerns
Topic7.Summary: Council members raised concerns about pothole repairs and snow and ice removal, citing safety and staffing constraints. Transportation staff said a community engagement process on snow removal is underway and that contractor and staffing capacity remain the main challenges.

Topic8.Title: Budget Review Process and Next Steps
Topic8.Summary: Council was asked to submit proposed budget changes by September 25 so staff can prepare the packet. The first reading is scheduled for October 5, with adoption planned two weeks later. Council members discussed the zero-sum nature of budget changes and the need to identify funding sources.
